landing.title: The Guided Planet
landing.standfirst: A free illustrated newspaper for children aged 7 to 12 and the grown ups who read with them. Every month: the good side of screens, and the judgement to go with it.
body: Issue 001 is The Curiosity Edition. Children's code heading for the space station. Young inventors who started with a person who needed help. What scientists actually know about screen time. Friendships that travel further. And Become the Algorithm, a paper game about who really chose the next video.
Twelve A4 pages, ready to print in colour or in an ink saver version, with an accessible online edition and every source listed in full.

school.subject: A free newspaper for your pupils: The Guided Planet, Issue 001
body: I am writing to share The Guided Planet, a free monthly newspaper for children aged 7 to 12 about the good side of screens.

Issue 001 covers ESA's Mission Zero (pupils' code running on the International Space Station, open until 22 March 2027), young inventors from Coolest Projects 2026, what the research says about different kinds of screen use, online friendship with safety qualifications, and a paper activity on recommendation algorithms that needs no devices or accounts.

Every page lists its sources. It is free to print, copy and share with your class. The algorithm activity touches the Education for a Connected World strand on managing online information for ages 7 to 11.
You are welcome to send it home with pupils or put it on your website.
school.signoff: Justin Phillips, Editor in Chief, The Guided Planet

social.linkedin:
We made a newspaper for children about the good side of screens.

Twelve pages. Free. No phone or account needed for any of the activities.

In Issue 001, children can plan a picture made of 64 lights for ESA's Mission Zero, where young people's code runs on the International Space Station. Last season 24,695 young people took part.

There is a page on what scientists actually know about screen time, with the limits printed next to the findings.

And there is a paper game called Become the Algorithm. One child picks a secret favourite. The other only sees what was watched and what was skipped. Five rounds later, the whole table is talking about how a recommendation gets made.

A delay is not preparation. This is one small way to prepare.

The download is in the first comment.
